radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Chronic skin and graft-versus-host disease of the lower
extremities, complaining of severe right Achilles pain, rule out tendinitis.

TECHNIQUE:  Images were acquired on a 1.5 Tesla magnet without intravenous
gadolinium.  Sequences acquired include axial proton-density, axial T2 fat
sat, sagittal T1, sagittal STIR, and coronal proton-density fat sat-weighted
sequences.

COMPARISON:  Bilateral foot radiographs ___.

FINDINGS:  At least some of the sequences are somewhat degraded by motion
artifact, nonetheless diagnostic images were obtained.

No fracture, dislocation, or gross degenerative change is detected about the
ankle joint.  There is minimal fluid within the joint, within physiologic
limits.  No marrow edema is detected about the joint.  There is no evidence of
an osteochondral lesion.

Visualized portions of the tendons and muscles crossing the ankle joint are
within normal limits in signal intensity and morphology.  There is extensive
edema of the plantar muscles including the abductor digiti minimi, quadratus
plantae and flexor digitorum brevis muscles.  The origin of the plantar fascia
is within normal limits, however.  The appearances suggest of nonspecific
edema within the muscle rather than plantar fasciitis.  No evidence of tendon
tear or degeneration about the ankle.  No tenosynovitis seen.

The tibiofibular, talofibular and calcaneofibular ligaments are well seen and
are intact.  The deltoid ligament is within normal limits.

No masses are detected within the tarsal tunnel.  The sinus tarsi is within
normal limits in signal intensity and morphology.  

There is mild subcutaneous edema overlying the Achilles tendon (7:15);
however, the tendon itself is normal in appearance.  No tendon tear.  No
tendon degeneration.  No edema of ___ fat pad.

There is diffuse thickening and edema of the skin. This is most marked over
the lateral aspect of the foot (4:21) however no fluid collections seen.

IMPRESSION:  
1.  Nonspecific edema of the plantar surface muscles of the foot.  No plantar
fasciitis.  
2.  The Achilles tendon is normal in appearance; however, trace subcutaneous
edema is seen overlying the tendon.
3.  Diffuse skin thickening and subcutaneous edema, more prominent over the
lateral aspect of the foot.  No fluid collections seen.
